source.title: Literate and illiterate world population
source.subtitle: Share of adults who can read and write a simple statement about their everyday life.
source.citation: UNESCO (1957) and other sources – with major processing by Our World in Data
source.fullCitation: UNESCO (1957); UNESCO (1953); Buringh and van Zanden (2009); van Zanden, J. et al.; UNESCO Institute for Statistics (2025) – with major processing by Our World in Data. “Literate” [dataset]. UNESCO, “World illiteracy at mid-century”; UNESCO, “Progress of literacy in various countries”; Buringh and van Zanden, “Charting the “Rise of the West”: Manuscripts and Printed Books in Europe, A Long-Term Perspective from the Sixth through Eighteenth Centuries”; van Zanden, J. et al., “How Was Life? Global Well-being since 1820 - Education 2014”; UNESCO Institute for Statistics, “UNESCO Institute for Statistics (UIS) - Education” [original data].
source.note:
Because definitions of literacy and population coverage changed over time, comparisons between historical and modern data
should be made with caution.
